ekegusii: Welwitscha (Welwitscha mirabilis) nigo kere ekemeri kiamete amatuko amatang’ani amwanyabanto, egekwama ase asinine ase ekengeka ki’enyancha ime ya Namibia na Angola ya maate. Welwitschia maene nigo ore omote korende tori kororekana boigo ekero okororekana ritang’ani. Ekemeri ekegima nigo kebwate ritina erimo rinene ribwate amato abere amanene akwama-aya akororekana buna ebisicha ebinene bieringete bikaba ebigare. Welwitschia ndire ekororekana buna egetunwa ki’eubi. Ekemeri eke nigo botambe kere ase engaki y’okomera (nonyen’enkaki y, obotobu) – eyio etari gokoreka mono ase ebimeri. Welwitschia n’ekemeri getari koibora gioka, igo ebimeri bibere (egesacha n’egekungu) mbiganeiri korosia entetere. Ebisicha nigo bire buna chichuba (buna biri bie chipaini gose chisikadi)bire gati gati y’amato. Chikoni chinsubati echikwerusekani ekero chiakinire korusia chinteretere chiabo chire chingusu, echio chigosiaru bwango n’embeo. Nigo chigotoka ase ekemeri egekoro gia Gnetophyta ebi bire oboiribwang’e ne chikonifa chikorokwa (Pinophyta). Gnetophyta ebwate ebisaku bitato ebing’ao ekero okorigereri okororekana kwabo: Gnetum lianas ebwate amato amororo, Ephedra – ebwate amagwa amona Welwitschia enyene. Welwitscha nigo yanyorete erieta riaye korwa ase omonyamete korwa Slovenia okorokwa Friedeich Welwitscha oomwaka o 1860. Welwitschia nkwama ere ase ebendera ya Namibia. Welwitscha nabo ekoigwana bwango n’ase are aomo mono.Tari buna nigo etegemeete embura mono naende nabo ekonyoraamache aisaine korwa ase amare agocha korwa nyancha. Aya n’amang’ana atakeire oinyore ekero okoyosimeka omote o Welwitschia. Esababu enene omote oyo o Welwitschia otari kwama buya n’ekero aobekeire amache amange egereogunda. Igo netakeire chintetere chiasimekea ase omochanga (wchinyeke chibe chimirimita 2–5 ase obogare) ekiagwera amarabaakogacha amache egeka gtari maya ase ogokinna kwaye. Netakeire Welwitschia eumoreru amache n’okorenda okonene gose ebekerwe omoika. Chintetere echikomera ase echuma eyemo. Nabo naende chirasimekwe chibekwe ase etirisa igoro chirigererie maate. Ekero ogosimeka Welwitscha, goika obe omoremereria mono ekiagera ekemeri eke nigo gekwama ng’ora mono nigo ere e dainosa ase ogokwana ekeene. Eise koegwa oborabu obonge moono amo n’amache amange, kemer eke ngekwama gekaokwe ogetige.
english: Welwitschia (Welwitschia mirabilis) is a unique plant found in the deserts of Namibia and Angola in Africa. Welwitschia itself is very strange because it only has two leaves throughout its life. The plant grows slowly and lives for a very long time, with some specimens living for over a thousand years, appearing like large, old piles. Welwitschia is a plant that survives through fog. The plant also has a strong stem (like a trunk, woody) - which does not branch like other plants. Welwitschia is a plant that grows from the ground, with its roots (deep and shallow) spreading widely to absorb moisture. The leaves are always green (even when they are old) and have many small ridges on them. This unusual plant can survive extreme heat and drought, and it stores water in its stem and roots. It belongs to the group of plants called Gnetophyta which are related to conifers (Pinophyta). Gnetophyta has three families with similar characteristics: Gnetum vines with shiny leaves, Ephedra - with branches resembling Welwitschia's stems. Welwitschia is named after the Austrian botanist Friedrich Welwitsch who discovered it in 1860. Welwitschia is also a symbol of Namibia. Welwitschia also tolerates harsh conditions and is able to live. It needs little rain but also endures strong winds from the ocean. These adaptations allow it to survive in the harsh environment of Welwitschia. A major reason this plant doesn't die is because it has deep roots that reach underground. Its roots spread wide (sometimes up to 2–5 meters wide) absorbing moisture from the soil. It takes Welwitschia a long time to grow and develop, but once established it becomes very strong. The root system is strong and helps support the plant. Also, it continues to grow slowly and remains stable for many years. To survive, Welwitschia relies heavily on fog, which provides moisture to the plant, even though it lives in a dry area. This plant is truly remarkable and shows how plants can adapt to survive in difficult environments.

english: Minto FM Kibagendi expressed his sadness over the ongoing struggles facing youth regarding access to funds and opportunities. The Director of Youth Affairs, Anthony Kibagendi expressed his sadness over the ongoing struggles facing youth regarding access to funds and opportunities. Kibagendi stated that the government is working to improve the lives of young people by providing them with access to Youth Fund resources and empowering them to start their own businesses so they can secure their future and obtain loans and grants, especially concerning the Youth Fund which aims to improve their livelihoods. Kibagendi also said that the county government is making great efforts to ensure that youth benefit from various development programs, with a target of 30 percent of government projects benefiting youth. english: Then Annas sent him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.

ekegusii: Bono ekiagera ogochika kw’omoruoti kwarenge ogotindi, na ase ayio omorero bw’eriko riria konya omentirwe obeire omonene mono, chimeme chi’omorero oria chigasamba na goita abanto baria barutete Sadaraka, na Meshaka, na Abedi‐Nego, ase omorero oria.
english: The king's command was so urgent and the furnace so hot that the flames of the fire killed the soldiers who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego,

ekegusii: Mobani onde tari okorete ogokora gwe chinguru chinene, na ogokora okonene, na ogw’okoondokia okwo Musa aorogetie ase amaiso ’Abaisraeli bonsi.
english: For no one has ever shown the mighty power or performed the awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.

ekegusii: Obaache emiaro eria korwa ase emekonge, oyeoome netahabu, nero emesa erabogorerigwe.
english: Make the poles of acacia wood, overlay them with gold and carry the table with them.

ekegusii: Erio noche korwa aase ao, agwo sugusu y’aare; nigo orache amo nabanto abange, bonsi bariinete chibarasi, bare omoganda omonene ore nabarwani esegi abange.
english: You will come from your place in the far north, you and many nations with you, all of them riding on horses, a great horde, a mighty army.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku bakayaigwa, bagatengechigwa ase omoondoko, omoichano na obororo bikabwata abamenyete Bofilisti.
english: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the people of Philistia.

ekegusii: Abanto baane bakorire amabe abere: bantigire inche inde ensoko y’amache amaya ay’obogima; bakunyire ebisima biabo bi’amache, ebisima biremogete, bitanyare kogacha amache nonya ng’ake.”
english: "My people have committed two sins: They have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and have dug their own cisterns, broken cisterns that cannot hold water.

ekegusii: Abanto bonsi bagacha koebereria Daudi arie endagera, korende Daudi agatiana, ogoteba, “Nyasae ang’e egesusuru bono na kogenderera onye nkoria endagera erioba ritaragwa.”
english: Then they all came and urged David to eat something while it was still day; but David took an oath, saying, "May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!"

ekegusii: Ase omotienyi o gatano na kabere ase omwaka oria, Isumaeli mosinto o Netania, mochokoro bw’Elisama, oyorenge omonto bw’enyomba y’obogambi na omoteneneri omonene igoro ase abanene barenge gokorera omoruoti, amo nabanto bande ikomi, bagacha ase Gedalia, mosinto bw’Ahikamu, agwo Misipa. Ekero barenge koria endagera amo bonsi agwo Misipa,
english: In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was of royal blood and had been one of the king's officers, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. While they were eating together there,

ekegusii: Ase ayio, aya naro Omonene agoteba igoro ya Yehoyakimu mosinto o Yosia, omoruoti bw’Abayuda: “Abanto tibakomoreera na gokwana: Obee! Momura ominto! Gose: Obee! Mosubati ominto! Onde tari oramoreere na gokwana: Obee! Omonene! Obee! Naki arenge omonene!
english: Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: "They will not mourn for him: 'Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!' They will not mourn for him: 'Alas, my master! Alas, his splendor!'

ekegusii: rikamotebia, “Tebia Rehoboamu, mosinto o Sulemani, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, otebie nabanto bonsi b’enyomba ya Yuda, na aba eya Benjamin, na abanto bande abatigari ng’a:
english: "Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, to the whole house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people,

ekegusii: Boigo Saulo agaita nomoro abanto bonsi barenge agwo Nobu, omochie bw’abakuani. Agaita abasacha, na abakungu, na abana amo nabwo bakogonka, ne chiombe, ne chitigere, ne ching’ondi.
english: He also put to the sword Nob, the town of the priests, with its men and women, its children and infants, and its cattle, donkeys and sheep.

ekegusii: Tiga omokori amabe atige chinchera chiaye, na oyo otari omoronge atige ebirengererio biaye. Omonto oyio tiga airane ase Omonene, nere amororere amabera, ee, ase Nyasae oito, ere namwabere kegima.
english: Let the wicked forsake his way and the evil man his thoughts. Let him turn to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him, and to our God, for he will freely pardon.

ekegusii: Nigo nkoinyora amatuko a kare, na korengereria igoro y’ogokora kwao gwonsi, naba nkona‐koiranerera emeremo y’amaboko ao.
english: I remember the days of long ago; I meditate on all your works and consider what your hands have done.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Sulemani) Nyasae, kae omoruoti okobua gw’okogamba buna aye okogamba, na omwana bw’omoruoti agambe ase oboronge buna aye.
english: Of Solomon. Endow the king with your justice, O God, the royal son with your righteousness.

ekegusii: omonene bw’omosomba oria nigo arache rituko atakagereti, na ensa atamanyeti;
english: The master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he is not aware of.

ekegusii: Moimokie Esanduku eye y’Omonene ase egari igoro, na emegwekano eria y’etahabu, moyebeke ase esanduku eng’ao ebeere ensemo y’Esanduku eria y’Omonene. Emegwekano eyio moyeirere Omonene ebe okoruegwa ase engencho y’okomocha okwo. Nyuma y’ayio motige Esanduku egende aase aye.
english: Take the ark of the LORD and put it on the cart, and in a chest beside it put the gold objects you are sending back to him as a guilt offering. Send it on its way,

ekegusii: akamotebia, “Igora ekebao kerochie moocha!” Yehoasi agakeigora. Erio Elisha akamotebia, “Rasa!” Nere akarasa. Elisha agakwana, “Omogwe bw’obobui bw’Omonene. Omogwe bw’obobui igoro y’Abasiiria. Aye norwanie Abasiiria agwo Afeki goika obasirie kegima.”
english: "Open the east window," he said, and he opened it. "Shoot!" Elisha said, and he shot. "The LORD's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram!" Elisha declared. "You will completely destroy the Arameans at Aphek."

ekegusii: “Benjamin nesese y’orosana ekoria mono, engaki ya mambia yaria ebi’obotwari bwaye, na engaki ya mogoroba bwatanana ebiasakoire.”
english: "Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder."

ekegusii: “Kwana n’Abalawi, obatebie: Ekero mokonyora ensemo ya ikomi korwa ase Abaisraeli, eria Omonene abaeire ebe eyaino, erio morusie ensemo ya ikomi y’okoruegwa okwo, moyerentere Omonene.
english: "Speak to the Levites and say to them: 'When you receive from the Israelites the tithe I give you as your inheritance, you must present a tenth of that tithe as the LORD's offering.

ekegusii: Ase ande onsi ase amang’ana ’ogochika koria kw’omoruoti konya ararigwe, Abayahudi bakaba nekerero ekenene mono; bakaba bakweng’ata, bakorera na kobokia amagombo. Abange babo bakaba beboyetie chigunia na beagete ribu.
english: In every province to which the edict and order of the king came, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing. Many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

ekegusii: Ninchene erieta riane rinene, erio riakoretwe rikaba eritachenegeti ase egati y’abanto b’ebisaku, erieta erio inwe mwakorete rikaba eritachenegeti ase egati yabo. Ekero ndeorokie ase amaiso abo ng’a nomochenu inde ase egati yaino, erio nario abanto b’ebisaku baramanye ng’a inche ninche Omonene. Nabo Omonene Nyasae atebire.
english: I will show the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, the name you have profaned among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Sovereign LORD, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes.

ekegusii: Obatebie ng’a aya naro Omonene agoteba: “Obobe nobwabo abakungu abwo bakobarera ebimoya bire namaebi, babisiba ase amaboko abo, naende babarera ebitambaa bagotuba emetwe y’abanto abake na abanene, erinde babarichania. Inee! Inwe abakungu aba, nigo mogochia korigia abanto baane na kobarichania, mobasirie, erinde inwe mogenderere koba moyo na kwenyorera ebitoki?
english: and say, 'This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Woe to the women who sew magic charms on all their wrists and make veils of various lengths for their heads in order to ensnare people. Will you ensnare the lives of my people but preserve your own?

ekegusii: Abanto baino kobarakoborie: Nase ki Omonene, Nyasae oito, atokoreire amang’ana aya onsi? Aye oiranerie ng’a inche natebire: Koreng’ana buna mwaonchokire mwantigire, naende mwasasimire chinyasae ching’ao aiga ase ense yaino, naboigo mogochia koba abasomba b’abanto abaao ase ense etari eyaino.”
english: And when the people ask, 'Why has the LORD our God done all this to us?' you will tell them, 'As you have forsaken me and served foreign gods in your own land, so now you will serve foreigners in a land not your own.'

ekegusii: Ekero omokungu oria agendererete gokwana nomoruoti, Nathani omobani agacha aroro agwo.
english: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, bogoria ebirwanero bionsi bia Nyasae, erinde monyare koamererania ase rituko ri’obobe, na komwaikeranirie onsi, motenene.
english: Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand.

ekegusii: Naboigo banyorete Isi‐Boseti oraire borere bwaye agwo ase akanyomba g’okorara bakamoika ang’e bakamoita, bakamobutora omotwe bakayoira; erio bakagenda ase obotuko bwonsi goetera ase enchera y’Ekerubo Ekiomo.
english: They had gone into the house while he was lying on the bed in his bedroom. After they stabbed and killed him, they cut off his head. Taking it with them, they traveled all night by way of the Arabah.

ekegusii: Omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli agateba, “Obobe nobwaito! Omonene otorangeirie intwe abaruoti batato atobeke ase amaboko Abamoabu.”
english: "What!" exclaimed the king of Israel. "Has the LORD called us three kings together only to hand us over to Moab?"

ekegusii: He also gathered together all the leaders of Israel, as well as the priests and Levites.
english: Daudi agasangereria abaraai bonsi b’Abaisraeli amo nabakuani na Abalawi.

ekegusii: Toi, omoruoti o Hamati, agachia koigwa ng’a Daudi obuire abarwani bonsi ba Hadadeseri,
english: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,

ekegusii: Ere nigo are Nyasae oirokire ase ekegambero ki’abachenu, bonsi abamoetanaine nigo bamoirogete.
english: In the council of the holy ones God is greatly feared; he is more awesome than all who surround him.

ekegusii: “Ntorete abana baito abaisia abatangi, ne chitugo chiaito chintangi ase abakuani abagokora emeremo ase enyomba ya Nyasae oito, buna erikire ase amachiko, torente ne chintangi chie chiombe, na echie chimbori, na echie ching’ondi.
english: "As it is also written in the Law, we will bring the firstborn of our sons and of our cattle, of our herds and of our flocks to the house of our God, to the priests ministering there.

ekegusii: Nigo akoa omokungu omogomba chinguru chi’okoibora, oba nomogoko ase enka yaye. Omonene atogigwe!
english: He settles the barren woman in her home as a happy mother of children. Praise the LORD.

ekegusii: ribaga ri’ogotegerera emegano y’Abayahudi, gose amachiko ’abanto aba bakoonchorana ekeene.
english: and will pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of those who reject the truth.

ekegusii: Omobaso na obotuko namobe nobwoba, na obogima bwaino nabobe ase emechando; inwe timogosemeria okoba kw’obogima bwaino ng’a mbogenderere.
english: You will live in constant suspense, filled with dread both night and day, never sure of your life.

ekegusii: abagaaka baria emerongo ebere na bane bagotung’ama ase obosio bwaye oyoikaransete ase ekerogo ki’obonene, na komosasima ere oyore moyo goika kare na kare. Barabwo nigo bakoruta chigutwa chiabo bosio bw’ekerogo keria ki’obonene, bagoteba,
english: the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne, and worship him who lives for ever and ever. They lay their crowns before the throne and say:

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae ore ogotooreka gwaito, ase ogokora kw’ogokumia ogotoigwa ase oboronge bwao; naye ore ogosemeria kw’abanto bamenyete ase ense, nonya ngoika chinsinyo chi’ense, na ase chinyancha chi’aare.
english: You answer us with awesome deeds of righteousness, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas,

ekegusii: Bono Festo gasoire ase obogambi bwaye, nyuma y’amatuko atato agatiira gochia Yerusalemu korwa Kaisaria.
english: Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,

ekegusii: ekiagera kwabeire nekeririanda na endamwamu asende. Aye kwambwatire na gwantugutire gochia aare.
english: because of your great wrath, for you have taken me up and thrown me aside.

ekegusii: Omochie oria nigo orenge omogare naende omonene, korende abanto barengeo nigo barenge abake ase omobaro, ne chinyomba konya tichiraagachwa imeo.
english: Now the city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it, and the houses had not yet been rebuilt.

ekegusii: Ayio tari amang’ana a bosa asemore, naro obogima bwaino; na ase okoigwera amang’ana aya namogenderere komenya engaki entambe ase ense eyio mogochia koira ng’umbu ya Yorodan.”
english: They are not just idle words for you-- they are your life. By them you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

Abagusii Customs XV: Amasabo Ye Ribina Omogaka sokoro ominto nantebetie buna Mwanyagetinge ominto omokoro naegenete ebinto gete, ebio ekero biakorekanire, egento gete nigo kegokorekana. Nabo kerabe ekiya gose ekebe. Ase rituko ria rero, tiga ingo toyakwanere amang'ana aria abakoro baito babegete okwegena ase are buna ekobwatia: 1. Ekiegesa: Ekero ekiegesa kiarenge koria omonto, nigo yarenge gotebekana ng'a aande aake omonto nare okare kogokwana. Na kogesiria, nigo kwarenge gotebigwa obare abana bamino ase omoyo ime, otari gokwana oigwekane !! 2. Gotamboka ebite bie ching'eni: Oise gotora ching'eni ebite erinde obitige inse omonto ache abitamboke, nigo ebianda bigokoria na ochake kominyoka ekero kwabekire ching'eni echi riiko, goikera gwachiyekire erinde gwachirire. 3. Naiguure bwatiokire: Oise kogenda mw' omwamate oo, omanye konyora buna okorire koragera naende n' ebinto bakoenia korwa emesa, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna aye nigo okare gokwana omoamate oyo oo bobe. Korende oise goika onyore nigo bagotereka endagera emesa baragere gose mbagasaine koragera, nigo egotebekana buna nigo ogokwana omwamate oyo buuya. 4. Oyo tata nakamura aranyore: Omosacha mokaye ebwateranetie n' egioto geise komocharoka okogoro, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna omorugie oye nigo agocha koibora omwana omomura. Kai tata !! Egioto giacharokire amagoro y' omogaka Simba Ndemo aaria Kisii Town, Kisii County. Tokare goika n' magokoro baba ominto aaria Barclays Bank, Kisii Town. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015 5. Endoto embe: Oise korota omonto orwarete buna ogwenire na konora nigo egotebekana ng'a endoto eye n' embe na nigo oyo arakwe. 6. Omwana ngoseka are: Omwana omoke ekero araire aise goseka, igo nigo yarenge kororekana buna nigo arota buna ise okuure. 7. Omwana nkorera are: Omwana omoke ekero araire aise korera karaire, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna nigo arota buna ng'ina okuure. 8. Oyo tata nigo arabe oundu: Oise gotamboka omwana nigo egotebekana buna omwana oyo tagokina atambee gochia igoro. 9. Oyo n' omogworu: Ekero omonto akorota oyomwabo buna okure nigo egotebekana buna nigo aragerete obotuko obuo akaigota kerage. 10. Eye yabeire ekeriero: Etwani iese kobuga chinsa chiri etabwenereti kobuga buna botuko gati, igo mbobe. Nigo yarenge gotebekana buna omonto bw' eamate eye nache atwe ekamo. Etwani buna eye nigo yarenge konyenywa ase obwango na koba ekeriero. Koru ase omogaka sokoro ominto, mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

These are the ones: Abagusii Culture And Customs CXXXIII: Is the wealth of a generous person diminished when he gives it away completely? Abagusii Culture And Customs XVI: Does a beautiful girl cause envy among those who aren't beautiful? Abagusii Customs XV: The Respect of Elders A father does not despise his children, even if they are troublesome; a mother doesn't reject her children, even if they make mistakes, she loves them just the same. But observe this important thing well. For sometimes, because of poverty, old people may fail to teach their children good manners: 1. Teaching: A lesson taught repeatedly to a child, will stick with him forever and he will never forget it. And remember, it is better to teach children while they are young, than to try to correct them when they are grown up!! 2. Avoiding bad company: It is good to choose good friends carefully so that a child doesn't associate with bad companions, because bad friends can lead to trouble and ruin a good reputation, making it difficult to restore it. 3. Being careful with advice: It is good to listen to wise counsel, and to be humble enough to accept correction and learn from others’ experiences, so that you don't think you know everything and become arrogant. Therefore, always listen and let them advise you properly, so that you won't regret it later when things go wrong. 4. A foolish elder should be respected: An elder who speaks carelessly and makes reckless decisions, should still be respected so that he doesn't mistreat a younger person. May God help us!! This story happened to the family of Mr. Simba Ndemo who lives in Kisii Town, Kisii County. Go and ask about it at Barclays Bank, Kisii Town. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015 5. Regarding dreams: If someone has a dream and interprets it correctly, then it is believed that the dream is true and will come to pass. 6. A child who cries a lot: A child who cries constantly, it is believed that he will grow up to be a thief. 7. A quiet child: A child who is very quiet, it is believed that he will grow up to be a liar. 8. That elder is stubborn: If someone takes a child to an elder, it is believed that the child will not improve unless he is disciplined. 9. And the maternal uncle: A child who goes to his maternal uncle seeking help, it is believed that he will find favor and receive assistance. 10. And the inheritance: Sometimes people fight over property and quarrel bitterly, leading to conflicts. It is believed that a person who steals another’s property will suffer consequences. Sometimes such a person will be cursed and lose his inheritance. Greetings to our fathers and mothers, goodbye everyone and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Abanto bonsi b’omochie bakarangerigwa kobabwatia, na kobabwatirie Yoshua, bakang’uswa gochia aare korwa ase omochie.
english: All the men of Ai were called to pursue them, and they pursued Joshua and were lured away from the city.

ekegusii: “Orende Rituko Rinene rie Chichuma, ase engencho y’ogotongora kw’engano, ne Rituko Rinene ri’Ogosangereria Rigesa, omoerio bw’omwaka.
english: "Celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.

ekegusii: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, "Take and eat; this is my body."
english: Kobakoragera, Yeso akabogoria omogati, akayosesenia, akayosamunyora, akaa aborokigwa, akabora, “Bogoria, morie; oyo noro omobere one.”

ekegusii: “Omonto omosacha aise konyorekana oraire nomokungu bw’omonto onde, bonsi babere, omosacha oria amo nomokungu oria, goika baitwe bakwe. Goika morusie obobe borue ase Abaisraeli.
english: If a man is found sleeping with another man's wife, both the man who slept with her and the woman must die. You must purge the evil from Israel.

ekegusii: “Ekerentane, gose omonto bw’ororeria rwaye, nonya ngoika ekiaare gia ikomi, tabaisa gosoa ase omosangererekano bw’Omonene.
english: No one born of a forbidden marriage nor any of his descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD, even down to the tenth generation.

ekegusii: Obwa ikomi na kane bokagwera Matitia; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: Korende ere agakana ase amasio abo bonsi, akabora “Timanyeti ayio ogokwana.”
english: But he denied it before them all. "I don't know what you're talking about," he said.

ekegusii: Sulemani akagamba agwo Yerusalemu igoro y’Abaisraeli bonsi ase emiaka emerongo ene.
english: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

ekegusii: Farao akairaneria, “Ng’ankio.” Musa akamotebia, “Nigo erabe buna gwateba, erinde omanye ng’a onde tari buna Omonene, Nyasae oito.
english: "Tomorrow," Pharaoh said. Moses replied, "It will be as you say, so that you may know there is no one like the LORD our God.

ekegusii: Omonto okona‐gokurerwa botambe ase okorongeigwa, korende okong’ia ebigoti, oyio nasirigwe mobosokano, tagokonywa.
english: A man who remains stiff-necked after many rebukes will suddenly be destroyed-- without remedy.

ekegusii: Naende agateba, “Omonene, Nyasae o Shemu, nasesenigwe, na Kanani abe omosomba oye.
english: He also said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the slave of Shem.

ekegusii: Oimokie etukia inke igo, oyesiberanie ase omokoba bw’eganchwa yao.
english: But take a few strands of hair and tuck them away in the folds of your garment.

ekegusii: Oboagacho obwarenge ao, ensemo ya bosongo, nigo bwarenge nobogare bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko emerongo etano na ebere. Obonetu bw’enyasi yonsi y’enyomba eria nigo bwarenge obw’ekerengo ki’amaboko atano, na obotambe bwaye amaboko emerongo kianda.
english: The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.

ekegusii: Abana abamura ba Raeli nabwo Yusufu na Benjamin.
english: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

ekegusii: Eliakimu na Maaseya, Miyamini na Mikaya, Elioenai na Zakaria, na Hanania, abarenge abakuani, bagatenena babwatete ebirombeta.
english: as well as the priests-- Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah and Hananiah with their trumpets--

ekegusii: Ezara, omworokia bw’amachiko, nigo atenenete igoro ase obotindiaro bwe chibao bwaroisetigwe ase emeremo eyio. Abatenenete ase ensemo yaye y’okorio nabwo aba: Matitia na Sema, Anaya na Uria, Hilikia na Maaseya. Na abatenenete ensemo yaye y’okobee, nabwo aba: Pedaya na Mishaeli, Malikia na Hasumu, Hasibadana na Zakaria, na Mesulamu.
english: Ezra the scribe stood on a high wooden platform built for the occasion. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah; and on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.

ekegusii: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
english: Pelatia, na Hanani, na Anaya;

ekegusii: Omoruoti akabairaneria, akabatebia, “Amang’ana aane tari koonchoka, na motantebeti chindoto chiane amo nengencho yaye, nigo morabutoranwe ekiimo ase ekiimo, ne chinyomba chiaino nchitagorwe chibe amatombe.
english: The king replied to the astrologers, "This is what I have firmly decided: If you do not tell me what my dream was and interpret it, I will have you cut into pieces and your houses turned into piles of rubble.

ekegusii: Titokoirana ase chinka chiaito goika torore ng’a Abaisraeli baminto banyorire kera omonto orogongo rw’omwando oye.
english: We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received his inheritance.

ekegusii: Nabeire ngokorigia ase Obomenyo Obochenu, erinde ndore okobua kwao na obonene bwao.
english: I have seen you in the sanctuary and beheld your power and your glory.

ekegusii: Abanto bonsi bagacha ase rinani, na aroro agwo bakarora obooke bore inse.
english: The entire army entered the woods, and there was honey on the ground.

ekegusii: Chibachwa chiane nigo chikoyia buna omorero, omobere one bwonsi orwarire.
english: My back is filled with searing pain; there is no health in my body.

ekegusii: Omonene nigo agoteba iga: “Ebirengererio biane tibiri buna ebiaino, gose chinchera chiaino tichiri buna echiane.
english: "For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways," declares the LORD.

ekegusii: Na Omonene akababeka ase amaboko ’Abaisraeli, nabarabwo bakabaumokera na kobaseria gochia Sidoni, omochie omonene, na Misirefoti‐Maimu, na goika ebate ya Misipa, ensemo ya moocha. Bakabaita; monto tatigara nonya noyomo.
english: and the LORD gave them into the hand of Israel. They defeated them and pursued them all the way to Greater Sidon, to Misrephoth Maim, and to the Valley of Mizpah on the east, until no survivors were left.

ekegusii: Korende nonya naboigo, aye tokonyara koagacha enyomba eyio otatiga omwana oo, omomura oria oraiborwe korwa ase enda yao, nere oraagachere erieta riane enyomba.
english: Nevertheless, you are not the one to build the temple, but your son, who is your own flesh and blood-- he is the one who will build the temple for my Name.'

ekegusii: Agacha asetore, akabogoria orokini rwa Paulo, agesibera amagoro na amaboko, akabora, “Omoika Omochenu otebire iga: Naboigo Abayahudi ba Yerusalemu barache gosiba omonto omonyene orokini oro, na barabwo nabamobeke ase amaboko ’abanto b’Ebisaku.”
english: Coming over to us, he took Paul's belt, tied his own hands and feet with it and said, "The Holy Spirit says, 'In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and will hand him over to the Gentiles.'"

ekegusii: Inwe mokaba abegi baito, na ab’Omonene, na nonya mwachandegete mono, mwanyorete ring’ana amo nomogoko okorwa ase Omoika Omochenu,
english: You became imitators of us and of the Lord; in spite of severe suffering, you welcomed the message with the joy given by the Holy Spirit.

ekegusii: Naboigo ase ensemo ya sugusu oroisie ebitambaa bire nobotambe bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko rigana erimo, bisiirwe ne chisiiro emerongo ebere, ne chinterekerero chiabo emerongo ebere chie chitaai. Ebigobanio amo ne chinuga chiabo bibe bie chifeta.
english: The north side shall also be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

ekegusii: Ekero Yoshua na Abaisraeli bonsi baroche ng’a abwo baboete babwatire omochie na koyosamba, bakairana, bagachaka goita abanto ba Ai.
english: For when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that smoke was going up from the city, they turned around and attacked the men of Ai.

ekegusii: Ase amatuko arache ekero orachiche korora eng’eria yane, oboronge bwane nabombere kirori. Kera embori etari nyankanga gose nyankororo, na kera emanwa y’engondi etari emwamu, onye ekonyorekana asende, oyebare ng’a eyio nigo eibire.”
english: And my honesty will testify for me in the future, whenever you check on the wages you have paid me. Any goat in my possession that is not speckled or spotted, or any lamb that is not dark-colored, will be considered stolen."

ekegusii: Ekero kwabisire obosio bwao, nigo bikoba nobwoba obonene; na ekero okobiura omoika obo, nigo bigokwa, biairana ase amaroba ime.
english: When you hide your face, they are terrified; when you take away their breath, they die and return to the dust.

ekegusii: mobasokie bonsi babere, mobaire isiko y’egeita ki’omochie, erio mobaake amagena bakwe. Omoiseke oria aitwe, ekiagera atakuurete akonywe, nonya orenge ase omochie ime, na omosacha oria, ekiagera atomana nomoiseke oriereirwe boko nomonto omoao. Goika morusie obobe borue asemore.
english: you shall take both of them to the gate of that town and stone them to death-- the girl because she was in a town and did not scream for help, and the man because he violated another man's wife. You must purge the evil from among you.

ekegusii: Amo nere bakabamba abauri babere, oyomo ensemo y’okoboko kwaye gw’okorio, na oyomo ensemo y’okoboko kwaye gw’okobee. [
english: They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.

ekegusii: Ase amatuko atano na rimo okore emeremo yao yonsi.
english: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

ekegusii: Erio Kaini akarua ase obosio bw’Omonene, akagenda, akamenya ase ense ya Nodi, moocha ya Edeni.
english: So Cain went out from the LORD's presence and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

ekegusii: Yonathani agatebia Daudi, “Saulo tata nigo aganetie kogoita. Ase ayio bwerende mono ankio mambia; ogende aase are bobisi, bwebise.
english: and warned him, "My father Saul is looking for a chance to kill you. Be on your guard tomorrow morning; go into hiding and stay there.

ekegusii: Nimbakore babe egesaku ekemo ase ense eyio, agwo ase ebitunwa bi’Abaisraeli. Omoruoti oyomo nabe okogambera bonsi. Tibakogenderera koba ebisaku bibere, gose gwatananeka babe amaruoti abere.
english: I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. There will be one king over all of them and they will never again be two nations or be divided into two kingdoms.

ekegusii: nabae obogima bwa kare na kare baria bakorigia obonene, na ogosika, na ogotasareka, na gokora amaya ase oboremereria.
english: To those who by persistence in doing good seek glory, honor and immortality, he will give eternal life.

ekegusii: Ase igo Abaisraeli bonsi bagatiga Daudi, bakabwatia Seba, mosinto o Bikiri; korende Abayuda bakabwatia omoruoti obo korwa Yorodan goika Yerusalemu.
english: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bicri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

ekegusii: When Ish-Bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel became alarmed.
english: Ekero Isi‐Boseti, mosinto o Saulo, aigwete ng’a Abineri oitirwe agwo Heburoni, akerusia moyo, na Abaisraeli bonsi bagaichana na gokumia.

ekegusii: Erio Abimeleki akarangeria Ibrahimu, akamoboria, “Inki eke gwatokoreire iga? Inki nakomocheire goika kwarentire igoro yane na igoro y’oboruoti bwane ebibe ebinene buna ebi? Gwankoreire amang’ana atagwenerete gokorwa.”
english: Then Abimelech called Abraham in and said, "What have you done to us? How have I wronged you that you have brought such great guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done."

ekegusii: Korwa ase chinsemo chionsi nigo tokomigwa, korende titori komigeka; iga togoichanigwa, korende titogokwa emioyo,
english: We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;

ekegusii: “Ase engaki eria tokaira ense y’abaruoti baria babere b’Abaamori, ense yarenge moocha y’orooche rwa Yorodan, gochakera orooche rw’Arinoni goikera egetunwa kia Herimoni.
english: So at that time we took from these two kings of the Amorites the territory east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Gorge as far as Mount Hermon.

ekegusii: Naki Melkizedeki oyio nigo arenge omoruoti o Salemu, omokuani o Nyasae Ore Igoro Mono. Ekero Ibrahimu are koirana korwa ase ogoita abaruoti, Melkizedeki akaumerana nere, akamosesenia.
english: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the defeat of the kings and blessed him,

ekegusii: Bakamoiraneria, “Yeso Omonazareti.” Yeso akabatebia, “Ninche ere.” Yudas nere oyomoruete nigo ateneine amo nabarabwo.
english: "Jesus of Nazareth," they replied. "I am he," Jesus said. (And Judas the traitor was standing there with them.)

ekegusii: Rora, nobwanchani bore naki, obwo Tata atoeire, ng’a torokwe abana ba Nyasae, na naboigo tore! Naki ekegerete ense etatomanyeti neke, ng’a temomanyeti ere.
english: How great is the love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him.

ekegusii: Goika bagachia komorora ng’umbu y’enyancha bakamoboria, “Omworokia, indi gwachete aa?”
english: When they found him on the other side of the lake, they asked him, "Rabbi, when did you get here?"

ekegusii: Enyorere obong’aini na okomanya, tobaisa kobieba! Tibwanga koigwera amang’ana ngokwana korwa ase omonwa one.
english: Get wisdom, get understanding; do not forget my words or swerve from them.

ekegusii: Na abakungu bagateba, “Ekero twasambete ubani na koumora okoruegwa gwaito gw’ekenyugwa ase Eting’ana ya Igoro, naende tokayeroiseria emegati yabekire omogwekano oye, abasacha baito nigo bancheranete nayio.”
english: The women added, "When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did not our husbands know that we were making cakes like her image and pouring out drink offerings to her?"

ekegusii: Ngosemeria ki omonto otamoirogete Nyasae abwate, ekero arakwe, ekero Nyasae aramoure obogima.
english: For what hope has the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

ekegusii: Na inwe namoruegwe nabaibori baino, na bamura bamino, na eamate yaino, na abasani baino, na barabwo nababeke abande baino ase ogoitwa.
english: You will be betrayed even by parents, brothers, relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death.

ekegusii: Bono Abaisraeli tibakonyara gokora buna barenge gokora agwo ritang’ani, tibakonyenyera ching’iti chi’ebing’wanso biabo orosana isiko; goika bachindetere inche Omonene, bachiire ase omokuani agwo ase egesoero ki’Eema y’Omosangererekano, bachinyenyereo chibe ebing’wanso bi’omorembe asende.
english: This is so the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they are now making in the open fields. They must bring them to the priest, that is, to the LORD, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and sacrifice them as fellowship offerings.

ekegusii: Obochore engoro gati gati, ase omotwe ogosoera, oyebeke ekenario buna egi’esati, techa gotandoka.
english: with an opening for the head in its center. There shall be a woven edge like a collar around this opening, so that it will not tear.

ekegusii: Korende Abisalomu agatoma abanto bobisi ase ebisaku bionsi bi’Abaisraeli babitebie, “Ekero moraigwe eriogi ri’egetureri, erio moake eriogi motebe: Bono Abisalomu obeire omoruoti o Heburoni!”
english: Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout the tribes of Israel to say, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpets, then say, 'Absalom is king in Hebron.'"

ekegusii: “Ekero narenge ase emechando, nigo nasabete Omonene, na ere akang’iraneria. Korwa ime ase enda y’aase abakure nigo narerete, aye Omonene okaigwa eriogi riane.
english: He said: "In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me. From the depths of the grave I called for help, and you listened to my cry.

ekegusii: You will seek me and find me when you seek me with all your heart.
english: Namondigie monyoore, komorandigie ne chinkoro chiaino chionsi.

ekegusii: Akarenta abakuani bonsi korwa ase emechie y’Abayuda, na ase ense yonsi korwa Geba goika Beeri‐Seba agakora aase onsi aimokererete igoro agwo ase abakuani barenge gosambera ubani akaba aatachenegeti. Na ebisasimero bi’aase aimokererete igoro arenge agwo ase ebiita bi’omochie, keria kiarenge ase egesoero ki’Egeita kia Yoshua, omotang’ani bw’omochie, na keria kiarenge ensemo y’okobee y’oyo ogosoera omochie, omoruoti akabitagora akabiyeria inse.
english: Josiah brought all the priests from the towns of Judah and desecrated the high places, from Geba to Beersheba, where the priests had burned incense. He broke down the shrines at the gates-- at the entrance to the Gate of Joshua, the city governor, which is on the left of the city gate.

ekegusii: Yoeli, mosinto o Sikiri, nere orenge omoteneneri obo; na Yuda, mosinto o Hasenua, akaba omoteneneri o kabere ase omochie oria.
english: Joel son of Zicri was their chief officer, and Judah son of Hassenuah was over the Second District of the city.

ekegusii: Akarigia korora Yeso, gose monto ki; ko tanyara ase engencho y’omoganda, ekiagera arenge omweng’e.
english: He wanted to see who Jesus was, but being a short man he could not, because of the crowd.

ekegusii: Rimumu erimo rikaba inse ya kera chinsagia ibere chigosoka korwa ase ritina. Ase ayio rikaba rimumu erimo inse ya kera orosagia rw’echio isano nemo chiroisirie chikaba egento ekemo ne ritina.
english: One bud was under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair-- six branches in all.

ekegusii: Rebeka nere akaimokia amaiso aye, akarora Isaka; erio agaika bwango korwa ase engamia igoro,
english: Rebekah also looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, Nyasae bw’Emeganda, igwa ogosaba kwane, tegerera onyigwe, aye Nyasae o Yakobo.
english: Hear my prayer, O LORD God Almighty; listen to me, O God of Jacob. Selah

ekegusii: Buna omonto oyo bw’amaroba arenge, naboigo nab’amaroba bare; na buna omonto o igoro are, naboigo naba igoro bare.
english: As was the earthly man, so are those who are of the earth; and as is the man from heaven, so also are those who are of heaven.

ekegusii: Na ase ekeng’wanso ki’omorembe akarua chieri ibere, ne chimingichi isano, ne chigoree isano, nechimanwa chimingichi isano chiakoorire omwaka oyomo. Oko nakwo kwarenge okorua gwa Pagieli, mosinto bw’Okirani.
english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old, to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ocran.

ekegusii: Ebikuba biabo nigo biaboirie chingobo chi’ebioma, na egeturi gie chimbaba chiabo nigo kiarenge buna egeturi gie chigari chinyinge chie chibarasi chikominyoka gochia ase esegi.
english: They had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the thundering of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.

ekegusii: Akarara naende, akarota eria kabere, akarora ebigara bitano na bibere ebinene ebinoru, bikinete ase oroboba oromo.
english: He fell asleep again and had a second dream: Seven heads of grain, healthy and good, were growing on a single stalk.

ekegusii: agateba, “Butorane omwana oyo ore moyo ebing’ese bibere, ekeng’ese ekemo keegwe omokungu oyomo, na ekende keegwe oyonde.”
english: He then gave an order: "Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other."

ekegusii: Omorembe nabatigeire; omorembe one nabaeire; tinkoyobaa buna ense ekoyobaa. Timoichana ase chinkoro chiaino, gose timoba nobwoba.
english: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled and do not be afraid.

ekegusii: Omonene nigo agoteba ng’a inwe moise kogenderera gokwana: Egurube y’Omonene, na kwanga koigwera, korende mogokwana amang’ana ayio Omonene abakanirie ng’a timobaisa gokwana bo,
english: Although you claim, 'This is the oracle of the LORD,' this is what the LORD says: You used the words, 'This is the oracle of the LORD,' even though I told you that you must not claim, 'This is the oracle of the LORD.'

ekegusii: Rigia Omonene amo ne chinguru chiaye, morigie mobe ase obosio bwaye botambe.
english: Look to the LORD and his strength; seek his face always.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, timobaisa gwancha Hezekia abang’aine, gose abasirie ase enchera eyio, na timobaisa komwegena, ekiagera enyasae ende y’egesaku kende gionsi, gose ey’oboruoti bonde, tiyana konyara gotooria abanto baye korwa ase okoboko kwane, gose korwa ase amaboko e chisokoro chiane. Nyasae oino nigo are bosa goetania chinyasae chiria; takonyara kobatooria korwa ase okoboko kwane!”
english: Now do not let Hezekiah deceive you and mislead you like this. Do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or the hand of my fathers. How much less will your god deliver you from my hand!"

ekegusii: Erio Belisasari akarua ogochika ng’a Danieli abekerwe eanga emonyinga, ne chisonoi chie chitahabu igoti riaye, na ararigwe ng’a ere nomogambi o gatato ase obogambi obo.
english: Then at Belshazzar's command, Daniel was clothed in purple, a gold chain was placed around his neck, and he was proclaimed the third highest ruler in the kingdom.

ekegusii: Inche Yakobo, omosomba o Nyasae na obw’Omonene Yeso Kristo, nabakwanirie inwe ab’ebisaku ikomi na bibere, abamwatananekire gochia chinse chire ao ao.
english: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes scattered among the nations: Greetings.

ekegusii: Orokerania ebibe biaino inwe ase inwe, na gosaberana, monyore okogwenigwa. Ogosaba kw’omonyene oboronge nigo kore nengencho enene mono gokorasabwe nomokia.
english: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man is powerful and effective.

ekegusii: Ibrahimu nigo akoorete emiaka rigana erimo, na emerongo etano na ebere, na etano (175), ase obogima bwaye.
english: Altogether, Abraham lived a hundred and seventy-five years.

ekegusii: Ee, abasomba baane mbabe bagotera bare nomosasoko ase chinkoro chiabo, korende inwe mobe mokorera more nobororo ase chinkoro chiaino, mobe mokweng’ereria ase omoika bw’omoichano.
english: My servants will sing out of the joy of their hearts, but you will cry out from anguish of heart and wail in brokenness of spirit.

ekegusii: Epafara oyore oyomo oino, omosomba o Kristo Yeso, obakwanirie. Ere okorire omokia ase okobainyora ase ogosaba kwaye, erinde monyare gotenena more abaikeranu, abamanyete mono ogwancha gwonsi kwa Nyasae.
english: Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, that you may stand firm in all the will of God, mature and fully assured.

ekegusii: Enyimbo y’obogambi tekorua o Yuda, gose omobeki amachiko ase ororereria rwaye, goika achiche oyo orabogorie obogambi, oyo abanto b’ebisaku bionsi baraigwere.
english: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs and the obedience of the nations is his.

ekegusii: “Rora, omonto oyo bwangete gokora Nyasae abe obotamero bwaye, nigo egenete obonge bw’obonda bwaye omonyene, na akeenenia ase chinguru chiaye chi’ogosaria.”
english: "Here now is the man who did not make God his stronghold but trusted in his great wealth and grew strong by destroying others!"

ekegusii: Ase ayio inche nkarengereria ng’a natugutirwe korwa ase obosio bwao, korende nindigererie naende gochia ase Hekalu yao Enchenu.
english: I said, 'I have been banished from your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'

ekegusii: Aye omonyene onachere ekina gi’okong’a oboronge, amaiso ao nigo akorora ayare ay’ekeene.
english: May my vindication come from you; may your eyes see what is right.

ekegusii: Musa akarambora okoboko kwaye, agaaka egetare keria nenyimbo yaye ara kabere. Amache agasoka amange mono, na omoganda oria okanywane chitugo chiabo chikanywa boigo.
english: Then Moses raised his arm and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water gushed out, and the community and their livestock drank.

ekegusii: Omonene nansibore korwa ase amabe onsi, na antoorie goika nsoe ase oboruoti bwa igoro. Ogotogigwa nokwaye kare na kare. Amina.
english: The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and will bring me safely to his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

ekegusii: "Teach me, and I will be quiet; show me where I have been wrong.
english: “Inyorokererie, na inche ninkire‐kiri imanyie amamocho nakorire.

ekegusii: Naki inche goetera ase amachiko nakwereire amachiko, erinde imbe moyo ase Nyasae.
english: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live for God.

ekegusii: Korende baminto, timorosa gokora amaya.
english: And as for you, brothers, never tire of doing what is right.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Ntwachiete n' omon'gina magokoro baba ominto aaria Masimba gokwania omosubati Pamela Bwari, oyio onyora abana chibarongo. Nche tinamanyete, korende go twaiika aroro, magokoro agantebia buna twaikeire korora Ekegusii gio okoibora abana chibarongo. Bono Ekegusii gi chibarongo nkereki? Baba ominto nigo atebete ng'a omong'ina ekero aiboire abana chibarongo nigo ekobetereria akorerane erinde tacha koirora koibora chibarongo naende. Ninki? Nche nigo natang'ang'ete. kobwatekana na magokoro, nigo abakoro bagoteba buna oise koibora chibarongo, togosieka roiboro. Nigo arenge koarama ase enyomba yaye ime! Nigo okoibora chibarongo naende. Kobwatekana n' ekemira giaito ntwe Mwanyagetinge, omokungu oiboire chibarongo nigo arenge koarama ase enyomba yaye ime, korwa abwo Ekegusii giachaka gokorwa! Korwa ase Abagusii abakoro, egware nigo yarenge ey' eng'encho mono. Nigo egware yare korentwa n' akayio! Abana chibarongo baikire aaria Masimba, nka bomame. Kera omonto nigo arenge gosia egware eye, bwetuna, omanya gotunia akamwana! Ritangani, ng'inarome chibarongo echi nigo are gocha ne chingo amo no obosie. Ase boigo, ng'ina koro korwa aaria ase aiboreire, nigo are gotoma chinkara echio chiare gosikwa amarwa. Amarwa aya nigo arenge gotubwa na amagoma. Bono ekero chibarongo chigosokigwa, nario amarwa aya arenge konywegwa. Bono mangana taraera. Nigo egware yare korigigwa. Ase boigo, nigo bare korigia omokorerani. Komenta nayio, nigo yare kobetereri nga bong'inarome nabarabwo nkoenga barenge amarwa. Bono rituko riria rigoika, chingo nachi chigotang'ana, bamanya gosoa nyomba baikaransa. Ko baikaransire, amarwa nigo arenge gokunorwa. Korwa abwo, omokorerani oika mbarabare na koyataoria na koa ng'ina koro asibe ritangani. Korwa abwo, abana aba chibarongo basokigwa isiko bamanya kogingerwa etuki! Obe! Egware eye yarentirwe na akayio n' eyaki? Mwana ominto naende mangana taraera. Ko abana aba chibarongo bagingeirwe, nigo egware yare korentwa n' akayio! Korwa abwo, omonto oegwa egware n' omwana. Kaeirwe omwana, nigo oyo arenge gosia egware eye, bwetuna, omanya gotunia akamwana! Egekorwa eke nigo kiarengenge goetanana ase kera omonto enyomba engima. Onye abanto bande barenge isiko, egware eye nigo yarenge gosokigwa ne chibarongo nario chiratunigwe na bari bare isiko. Go kera oyomo atunire, amarwa nigo arenge kobekwa amache, na abako basiba bamanya gosoka naro isiko. Goika omokorerani arenge koegwa esani amo n' eyanga. Omokorerani kagokora omoyega oyo, nigo arenge koegwa esani, amo n' eyanga. Korwa abwo, omanya kogenda, na abageni baruo bagenda. Nonya nabo igo, Ekegusii g' chibarongo tikiare koera bwango igo. Yaya. Buna bakona gokina, Ekegusii gete ngokorwa kiarenge. Bono nindi ngocha kogenda bomame? Yaya mwana. Kogenda bonyokorome tikoiyo. Aaiga naende, goika abaigwa baraganya, goikera Ekegusii gete, naende gekorwe! Ritangani, chibarongo nigo chiagakinire chitari kogenda bong'inarome! Yaani manya! Korende ekero chiaisanire gochia maguta motwe, nigo chiagakobirwe gochia bong'inarome. Bono oyo orenge kobakoba tari onde bwensi. Yaya. Ori orenge kobakoba nori bakorwa nyuma. Ko yaikire engaki y' okogenda bongina rome, nigo abana aba chibarongo barenge koegwa embori amo n' obosi, erinde betweka gochia abwo bong'inarome. Ko baikire geita, nigo barenge gotenena! Onye na abamura, n' omomura ogocha kobarotota! Onye n' abaiseke, n' abaiseke boigo! Bono rende onye chibarongo echi chiarenge omomura n' enyaroka? Ninki kiare koba? Onye abana aba chibarongo barenge omomura n' enyaroka, oyo okobarotota n' omomura n'enyaroka! Bono oyo okobarotota nigo arenge gotaoria obosi obo n' ekemunu, obotang'ani korwa geita. Ori otanganete gosoka ase okoiborwa nere okoegwa obosi. Ngina koro korwa abwo bonginarome, omanya kobwata obosi obo, otang'ana nyomba. Ng'ina koro korwa aaria bonginarome goika arusie obosie n' ekemunu! Gaikire nyomba, ngina koro oyo nigo arenge korigereria gochia isiko. korwa abwo, nigo ngina koro oyo arenge korusia obosi n' ekemunu, orusia oruta gochia ase omotobwa (omote ori okobera gesieri). Emeremo ya ngika koro teraera. Nigo ng'inakoro naende arenge korusia obosi bonde, omanya kobatunia ase obosio. Korwa abwo, obosi bwensi bwairwa nyomba. Bono ko baikire nyomba, baegwa amarwa ari ng'ina chibarongo atomete. Nigo amarwa aya arenge koigorwa, bataorerigwa baegwa banywe. Tari igo rioka. Nigo embori eri ngina chibarongo atomete yarenge konyenywa. Korwa abwo, bamanya kobekerwa ebitwanga, barara. Maambia yaye, bairana sobo n' embori egochia gosarara! Korwa abwo, abana aba chibarongo bamanya koirwa bware. Magokoro baba ominto nigo agoteba buna eke nakio kiarenge Egekoro kia Mwantagetinge, gi' chibarongo. Bwatera abwo goikera chingaki chinde, and thank you for listening.
english: These are the words: We have received news about the passing of our esteemed mother, Mrs. Masimba Gekwania Omisubati Pamela Bwari, who was known for raising children well. We didn't know, yet we continued praying, hoping her heart would recover so she could continue speaking the Ekegusii language and raising children properly. What does Ekegusii and proper upbringing mean? Our mothers always said that teaching children good morals is more important than just sending them to school to learn how to be raised correctly. Why? Because I understand. It pains my heart, but elders say that if you teach a child good morals, they will never stray from the right path. It is truly a difficult situation! Continuing to raise children properly. Remembering the teachings of our grandmother, Mwanyagetinge, a woman who raised children well, it is a difficult situation indeed, because Ekegusii customs are being forgotten! For the sake of our ancestors, let us maintain our traditions. Let us hold onto our culture! Children should emulate Mrs. Masimba, like their mothers. In the past, it was considered honorable to uphold our traditions, to respect and cherish our heritage! Friends, this message about upbringing has touched me deeply. Truly, those who were raised well are blessed, and they remember their roots and don't forget where they came from. These memories are precious and should be cherished. But what happens when a tradition is abandoned, and these memories fade away? What can we do to restore things? Let us strive to ensure that this upbringing continues, so that future generations also benefit. Those who were raised well often return to help others, remembering the lessons they learned. These lessons are valuable and should be passed on. Let us support those who are trying to rebuild. Let us embrace those who are working hard to improve things. Remember, it is better to encourage and uplift each other rather than criticize. This time of hardship teaches us the importance of unity and cooperation. Those who are rebuilding deserve our support and encouragement. Because of this, let us work together and offer assistance wherever possible, ensuring that everyone benefits. Because of this, children need guidance and protection so they don't lose their way! Oh! Is this tradition being lost due to negligence and carelessness? Another message touches me deeply. For the sake of these children, let us hold onto our culture! Because of this, parents should instill values in their children. Teach your children, and it will be considered honorable to uphold our traditions, to respect and cherish our heritage! The current generation needs to come together and address this issue seriously. Anyone who disrespects our traditions deserves condemnation, and their actions should be corrected by those who value our heritage. To honor our ancestors, let us preserve our memories and ensure that our traditions endure. Let us assist those who are striving to revive our culture and traditions. Let us appreciate those who are making an effort, and support them wholeheartedly. Because of this, let us move forward with determination, and welcome visitors with open arms. However, let us remember that Ekegusii and its upbringing should remain strong and unwavering. Amen. May they find strength and resilience, and may Ekegusii flourish forever. What is preventing us from moving forward? Yes, my child. Let us overcome obstacles and persevere. It is said that when people gather, they share ideas and strengthen bonds. Let us revitalize Ekegusii and make it thrive once more! Let us unite and work towards progress, ensuring that future generations continue to benefit from our rich cultural heritage! Truly I say! Let us carefully examine the root causes of our problems and seek solutions. Let us address the issues that hinder our progress. These efforts won't be easy, but they are necessary. Amen. Some may fail along the way, but let us learn from their mistakes. If we want to see positive change, let us guide our children with wisdom and compassion, teaching them to avoid the pitfalls of the past. Let us inspire them to become responsible citizens who contribute to society! Anyone with enemies should reconcile with them! Anyone with grievances should forgive! What makes someone abandon their family and community? What is the reason for such abandonment? Anyone who abandons their family and community faces consequences and regrets! These consequences involve losing blessings and opportunities, hindering progress. Some may start well but falter later. It is important to remember that true success comes from perseverance and dedication. This is why it is crucial to maintain integrity and honesty in all our endeavors! Let us remember our roots, because neglecting our traditions leads to decline. Because of this, let us safeguard our values and pass them down to future generations, preserving our identity and heritage (our customs are what define us). The results of this effort will be evident. This is why we must strive to uphold our principles, ensuring that our actions align with our beliefs. We must remain steadfast in our commitment to progress, embracing innovation while honoring our traditions. Let us move forward together, working towards a brighter future for all! Let us embrace unity, recognizing that collective action yields greater rewards than individual pursuits. Our hearts, filled with love and compassion, offer praise to God for the gift of life and the strength to overcome challenges, through unity. Let us dedicate ourselves to building a better world, guided by faith and gratitude, and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Erio abakungu baria abasomba bagasuka gochia ang’e, kera oyomo nabana baye, bagatung’ama inse.
english: Then the maidservants and their children approached and bowed down.

ekegusii: If he comes suddenly, do not let him find you sleeping.
english: tacha ababosokane, abanyore mwararire.

ekegusii: Naende nkarigereria, nkarora omonto obwate engori y’okorengera ase okoboko kwaye.
english: Then I looked up-- and there before me was a man with a measuring line in his hand!

ekegusii: Ekero ense eria egendererete koba amatongo netimoke ogotimoka okwo motayeete ekero mwamenyeteo.
english: All the time that it lies desolate, the land will have the rest it did not have during the sabbaths you lived in it.

ekegusii: Amang’ana aya naro akoregete ase amatuko ’Ahaswero, Ahaswero oyio akaba okogambera chingongo rigana erimo, na emerongo ebere, na isano na ibere (127), gochakera India goikera Etiopia.
english: This is what happened during the time of Xerxes, the Xerxes who ruled over 127 provinces stretching from India to Cush:

ekegusii: Na endagera eye egachwe eche koegwa abanto emiaka eye etano na ebere y’enchara, erache gocha ase ense ya Misiri, abanto tibabaisa gocha gosira ase enchara eyio.”
english: This food should be held in reserve for the country, to be used during the seven years of famine that will come upon Egypt, so that the country may not be ruined by the famine."

ekegusii: We have endured much ridicule from the proud, much contempt from the arrogant.
english: Twaichoirwe necheche y’abwo beisanekerete, na ogochaywa kw’abamwenu.

ekegusii: Korende tibaigwera Musa; abande bagatigaria eyende goika rituko ria kabere, na mambia yaye bakayenyora yagundire na yasoirwe namakonde, na Musa akababea mono.
english: However, some of them paid no attention to Moses; they kept part of it until morning, but it was full of maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.

ekegusii: Tindi gotiga aya gwachikire, ekiagera naye kwanyorokereirie.
english: I have not departed from your laws, for you yourself have taught me.

ekegusii: "You are my war club, my weapon for battle-- with you I shatter nations, with you I destroy kingdoms,
english: “Aye nenturago na ekerwanero kiane gi’esegi; goetera asore ning’ake ebisaku bibe ebisamunye, ninsirie amaruoti.

ekegusii: Seti nigo akoorete emiaka amagana kianda, na ikomi na ebere (912), erio agakwa.
english: Altogether, Seth lived 912 years, and then he died.

ekegusii: Husamu nere agakwa, na Hadadi, mosinto o Bedadi, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye; oyo nere obuete Abamidiani, ase ense ya Moabu na omochie oye nigo ore korokwa Aviti.
english: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, succeeded him as king. His city was named Avith.

ekegusii: Samweli akarara goika mambia; erio akaboka, akaigora ebisieri bi’enyomba y’Omonene. Ere akoboa gotebia Eli okorora koria aroche.
english: Samuel lay down until morning and then opened the doors of the house of the LORD. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,

ekegusii: “Ekiagera Abaefraimu beagacheire ebisasimero ebinge bikogera bakore ebibe, ebio biabeire ebibe asebare.
english: "Though Ephraim built many altars for sin offerings, these have become altars for sinning.

ekegusii: Korende baminto, nimbamanyie ng’a amang’ana aria onsi anyorete, abeire ase okogendereria gw’enchili.
english: Now I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has really served to advance the gospel.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae bw’Emeganda, karakune ense, ero nigo ekonyititoka, na ebitongwa bionsi bireo bibe bikorera. Ense engima neimokererigwe igoro, naende eiranigwe inse, buna orooche rwa Naili rore agwo Misiri.
english: The Lord, the LORD Almighty, he who touches the earth and it melts, and all who live in it mourn-- the whole land rises like the Nile, then sinks like the river of Egypt--

ekegusii: Yehu akaimoka, agasoa enyomba, na omobani oria omosae akaumora amaguta aria igoro ase omotwe o Yehu, akabora, “Aya naro Omonene, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, agoteba: Inche nagoakire amaguta obe omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, abanto baane.
english: Jehu got up and went into the house. Then the prophet poured the oil on Jehu's head and declared, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I anoint you king over the LORD's people Israel.

ekegusii: Ase ayio bono, inwe abanto momenyete Yerusalemu, na inwe Abayuda, nababoririe monache ekina ase egati yane na omogondo one.
english: "Now you dwellers in Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.

ekegusii: ee, arikwe nekaramu eroisirie korwa ase risasi, ekioma egekong’u, amang’erwe ase egetare abeo kare na kare.
english: that they were inscribed with an iron tool on lead, or engraved in rock forever!

ekegusii: “Omonene nabarentere okoragererigwa, na obotantanu, na emechando ase emeremo yaino yonsi mogokora, goika mosirigwe na koera bwango ase engencho y’ogokora kwaino okobe, na ekiagera mwantigire inche.
english: The LORD will send on you curses, confusion and rebuke in everything you put your hand to, until you are destroyed and come to sudden ruin because of the evil you have done in forsaking him.

ekegusii: Korende asende inche, nigo ere buya mono kobeera ang’e na Nyasae. Omonene Nyasae obeire obotamero bwane, ninyare koraria emeremo yaye yonsi.
english: But as for me, it is good to be near God. I have made the Sovereign LORD my refuge; I will tell of all your deeds.

ekegusii: Omonto omotaka nigo akogechwa nabanto bamwabo bonsi, gose tikori ogokumia ng’a abasani baye bamotigire. Nigo egenete amang’ana abo, ko aba bosa asare.
english: A poor man is shunned by all his relatives-- how much more do his friends avoid him! Though he pursues them with pleading, they are nowhere to be found.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, Omonene akaonchora ebirengererio biaye, agateba, “Ayio bono takoba bo.”
english: So the LORD relented. "This will not happen," the LORD said.

ekegusii: Natianire ng’a ning’ikeranie eira eyio yane; nimbwatie aya onsi gwachikire ase oboronge.
english: I have taken an oath and confirmed it, that I will follow your righteous laws.

ekegusii: Akamotebia, “Tiga abakure batindeke abakure babo, korende aye genda orandie oboruoti bwa Nyasae.”
english: Jesus said to him, "Let the dead bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim the kingdom of God."

ekegusii: Korende abanto aba nigo bakorama ase amang’ana onsi batamanyeti, na ase amang’ana bamanyete botambe koreng’ana buna ching’iti chitari nobong’aini chimanyete; ase aro besaria abanyene.
english: Yet these men speak abusively against whatever they do not understand; and what things they do understand by instinct, like unreasoning animals-- these are the very things that destroy them.

ekegusii: Nigo arenge kogenda ase omoruoti chingaki chia mogoroba, erio ase rituko ria kabere mambia oirana gochia ase enyomba ende y’abakungu inse y’oborendi bwa Saasigasi, oyorenge omoteneneri bw’abakungu ba sere‐sere b’omoruoti. Tarenge koirana gochia ase omoruoti eria kabere, otatiga onye omoruoti ogogetigwe nere, naende aba okomorangeria ase ogwatora erieta riaye.
english: In the evening she would go there and in the morning return to another part of the harem to the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who was in charge of the concubines. She would not return to the king unless he was pleased with her and summoned her by name.

ekegusii: abanto abwo netongeire, erinde bararie ogotogigwa kwane.”
english: the people I formed for myself that they may proclaim my praise.

ekegusii: Chinyama chionsi tichiri echimo; korende echinde nechia mwanyabanto, echinde nechie ching’iti, echinde nechie chinyoni, na echinde nechie chinswe.
english: All flesh is not the same: Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another and fish another.

ekegusii: Ekero endamwamu yaye erakee, na ere ebire aya kwamokorerete, erio nintome abanto bache gokorangeria oirane korwa aroro. Nase ki ndakwerwe nainwe mwensi babere ase rituko erimo.”
english: When your brother is no longer angry with you and forgets what you did to him, I'll send word for you to come back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?"

ekegusii: Then thundered the horses' hoofs-- galloping, galloping go his mighty steeds.
english: Erio chibarasi chiare gotitiria nebitaago biabo, chituoni chiachiriinete chiare gocharara‐charara.

ekegusii: Abana babo mbabe abange buna kare, omoganda obo nonyore chinguru ase obosio bwane, abwo bakobachanda, nimbae egesusuro.
english: Their children will be as in days of old, and their community will be established before me; I will punish all who oppress them.

ekegusii: Emechie banyorete ase omwando obo nero: Beeri‐Seba, na Seba, na Molada,
english: It included: Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,

ekegusii: Nigo okorera nobororo botuko bokia, na amariga nigo agoiteka ase chimboto chiaye; ase abanchi baye bonsi onde tari okomoremia; abasani baye bamong’ainire, babeire ababisa baye.
english: Bitterly she weeps at night, tears are upon her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is none to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.

ekegusii: So God has taken away your father's livestock and has given them to me.
english: Naboigo Nyasae akarusia etugo ya iso, akang’a inche.

ekegusii: Omonto onde oino karabe ne ring’ana ase oyomwabo, Inee, nare noboremu amosoere ase abwo batari abaronge? Inki rende atari komosoera ase obosio bw’abachenu?
english: If any of you has a dispute with another, dare he take it before the ungodly for judgment instead of before the saints?

ekegusii: Erio Musa agatebia Haroni, “Suka gochia ang’e ase egesasimero, na orue ekeng’wanso kiao ki’ebibe na eki’ogosambwa, okore okobwatanigwa asore aye omonyene, na ase abanto, erinde mwaberwe. Naende orue ekeng’wanso ekio abanto barentire, na okore okobwatanigwa asebare, buna Omonene achigete.”
english: Moses said to Aaron, "Come to the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and your burnt offering and make atonement for yourself and the people; sacrifice the offering that is for the people and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded."

ekegusii: Bono nigo yarenge engaki ye rigesa, na Yorodan nigo rwaichire mono namache aetanetie chingegu. Ekero abakuani, abwo babogoretie Esanduku eria, baigete Yorodan na batachete amache namagoro abo,
english: Now the Jordan is at flood stage all during harvest. Yet as soon as the priests who carried the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water's edge,

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Omonene, ngoika ririri oragenderere konyeba? Ngoika kare na kare? Ngoika ririri orabe kobisete obosio bwao ng’a tondora?
english: For the director of music. A psalm of David. How long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?

ekegusii: Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."
english: Pilato akairaneria, “Aya narikire, narikire.”

ekegusii: Abalawi bagakora buna Musa abatebetie, na abanto chilifu isato bagaitwa ase rituko erio.
english: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people died.

ekegusii: Agwo Abineri agakwana nabagaaka b’Abaisraeli, akabora, “Korwa ase chingaki chinde chiaetire mwabeire mokogania ng’a Daudi abe omoruoti oino.
english: Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, "For some time you have wanted to make David your king.

ekegusii: Nonya nomokungu oiborete abana batano na babere, nigo akogireka ase omoichano; erioba ri’obogima bwaye riagure kobore mobaso, osookigwe na goichanigwa. Nindue abatigari baitwe nemioro y’ababisa babo”. Nabo Omonene atebire.
english: The mother of seven will grow faint and breathe her last. Her sun will set while it is still day; she will be disgraced and humiliated. I will put the survivors to the sword before their enemies," declares the LORD.

ekegusii: Abanto bonsi b’ororeria rwa Israeli mbanyore oboronge na gwetogia ase Omonene.”
english: But in the LORD all the descendants of Israel will be found righteous and will exult.

ekegusii: Ekero aikaransire ase ekerogo ki’obonene ase oboruoti bwaye, ’arente ebuku y’amachiko korwa ase abakuani Abalawi, naende arike amang’ana ayio ayio ase ebuku ende.
english: When he takes the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself on a scroll a copy of this law, taken from that of the priests, who are Levites.

ekegusii: “Inee! Nyasae tari aaria igoro mono? Rigereria ching’enang’eni chia igoro buna chire aare mono!
english: "Is not God in the heights of heaven? And see how lofty are the highest stars!

ekegusii: Aya namaroro Isaya, mosinto bw’Amosi, aroche igoro y’ense y’Abayuda na omochie o Yerusalemu ekero Usia, na Yotamu, na Ahasi, na Hezekia, barenge abaruoti ase ense y’Abayuda.
english: The vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

ekegusii: Naki getongwa kende tikeri getari maiso marore asare, korende ebinto bionsi nigo bire aarabu naende bimaanoire ase amaiso aye, ere oyo torache koa omobaro.
english: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight. Everything is uncovered and laid bare before the eyes of him to whom we must give account.

ekegusii: They left the Desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
english: Bakarua erooro ya Sini, bakagenda bagaika Dofuka, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Omonene akamoiraneria, “Ning’o oete mwanyabanto omonwa? Ning’o omokorete abe rimama, gose omotino, gose abe okorora, gose omouko? Inee! Tari inche Omonene?
english: The LORD said to him, "Who gave man his mouth? Who makes him deaf or mute? Who gives him sight or makes him blind? Is it not I, the LORD?

ekegusii: “Aye Yonathani ominto, nigo inde nomoichano omonene ase engencho yao, aye nigo konya ongogetie mono. Obwanchani bwao nigo bwarenge bongogetie kobua obwanchani bw’abakungu.”
english: I grieve for you, Jonathan my brother; you were very dear to me. Your love for me was wonderful, more wonderful than that of women.

ekegusii: “Ekeene nabatebirie: Ebibe bionsi mwanyabanto nabaaberwe, na okorama gwonsi bararame,
english: I tell you the truth, all the sins and blasphemies of men will be forgiven them.

ekegusii: Ase engencho eyio Nyasae akabatiga batunyane okogania kwabo kw’obosooku, goika abakungu babo bakaonchoreria okomenyana kw’omobere kwa boronge ase oko gotari kwa boronge.
english: Because of this, God gave them over to shameful lusts. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

ekegusii: Put into it the pieces of meat, all the choice pieces-- the leg and the shoulder. Fill it with the best of these bones;
english: Obeke ebitari bie chinyama imeo, bionsi ebire ebiya, ekenama ne rireko, oyeichorie amauga, ochore ayare amaya.

ekegusii: Chinyoni nigo chikomenya ang’e na chirochio, nigo chikoba chigotera ekero chigwete ase chinsagia chi’emete.
english: The birds of the air nest by the waters; they sing among the branches.

ekegusii: agantebia: Inche ninkomente, na oroiboro rwao robuche goika robe emeganda y’ebisaku. Ning’ee ororeria rwao rorache korwa nyuma yao ense eye ebe omwando obo kare na kare.
english: and said to me, 'I am going to make you fruitful and will increase your numbers. I will make you a community of peoples, and I will give this land as an everlasting possession to your descendants after you.'

ekegusii: Ekerogo keria ki’oboruoti nigo kiabwate ekeriinero kiarenge nebitambokero bitano na ekemo, na egeteni ki’amagoro kiaroisirie korwa ase etahabu; bionsi nigo biabwatanirie nekerogo keria. Kera ensemo y’ekerogo mbiarengeo ebisiirero ase arenge gotoorera amaboko, na emegwekano ye chindo ebere yatenenirieo, oyomo ase kera ensemo.
english: The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold was attached to it. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing beside each of them.

ekegusii: Huramu, omoruoti o Turo, akairaneria ase rirube atomete ase Sulemani, rigoteba: “Ekiagera Omonene anchete abanto baye, okobekire aye koba omoruoti igoro asebare,”
english: Hiram king of Tyre replied by letter to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you their king."

ekegusii: Ekero Yoshua atebetigwe ng’a abaruoti baria barorekanire bebisete agwo ase rikuruma riria,
english: When Joshua was told that the five kings had been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah,

ekegusii: Rora, enda yane nigo enga buna edivai ekunekire mono, buna ebirandi biroisirie korwa ase amasankwa amayia bire ang’e kworeka.
english: inside I am like bottled-up wine, like new wineskins ready to burst.

ekegusii: Elikana nabwate abakungu babere, Hana na Penina. Penina nabwate abana, korende Hana tabwate bana.
english: He had two wives; one was called Hannah and the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Kiriati‐Yearimu bagacha, bakaira Esanduku eria y’Omonene, bakayebeka ase enyomba y’Abinadabu, ase ekegoro igoro; bagachora na gwatanana Eleazari, omwana oye omomura, abe okorenda Esanduku eria.
english: So the men of Kiriath Jearim came and took up the ark of the LORD. They took it to Abinadab's house on the hill and consecrated Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the LORD.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oo, oyomenyete ase egati yao, nigo are omorwani etuoni okogotooria. Ere nigo akogokerete nomogoko omonene. Nabe okirete‐kiri ore nobwanchani bwaye; akogokere nogotera kw’omogoko.”
english: The LORD your God is with you, he is mighty to save. He will take great delight in you, he will quiet you with his love, he will rejoice over you with singing."

ekegusii: Na rora, oyomo obo bw’abarenge amo na Yeso akarambora okoboko kwaye, akang’usa omoyio oye o birende, agaaka omosomba bw’omokuani omonene, akamobutora ogoto.
english: With that, one of Jesus' companions reached for his sword, drew it out and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

ekegusii: Inche namanyire ogosaria kwane, na ebibe biane nigo bire bosio bwane botambe.
english: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.

ekegusii: Bairire chibesa chionsi chianyorekanete ase enyomba y’Omonene, na bachibekire ase amaboko ’abateneneri b’emeremo amo nabakori emeremo.”
english: They have paid out the money that was in the temple of the LORD and have entrusted it to the supervisors and workers."

ekegusii: Omonto oyio akaroka kera eng’iti egotugwa, na kera enyoni ekoiruruka, na kera eng’iti y’orosana erieta riaye. Korende tarorekana mokonyi onde, barakonyane nere.
english: So the man gave names to all the livestock, the birds of the air and all the beasts of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.

ekegusii: Rora, Esanduku ere ne chibao chirikire oborori bw’okobwatana, eyio y’Omonene bw’ense engima, nkwambokigwa ere gochia rooche ng’umbu, bosio bwaino.
english: See, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will go into the Jordan ahead of you.

ekegusii: Esegi egatuboka naende, na Daudi akagenda korwania Abafilisti, akababua obobui obonene mono. Barabwo bagatama korwa asare.
english: Once more war broke out, and David went out and fought the Philistines. He struck them with such force that they fled before him.

ekegusii: Aye ense yonsi, aka eriogi ri’omogoko ase Omonene, tera ogotera kw’omogoko na motogie ase amariogi amanene.
english: Shout for joy to the LORD, all the earth, burst into jubilant song with music;

ekegusii: Korende aase aimokererete igoro tarusetigweo. Nonya naboigo, ase obogima bwaye bwonsi Asa nigo arenge nenkoro y’obwegenwa ase Omonene.
english: Although he did not remove the high places, Asa's heart was fully committed to the LORD all his life.

ekegusii: Ase ayio Omonene akaigwa ogosaba gwa Hezekia, akarorera abanto amabera.
english: And the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

ekegusii: Then Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting,
english: Musa na Haroni bagacha bosio bw’Eema eria.

ekegusii: Nyuma y’amatuko atano na atato aborokigwa baye nao barenge naende ase enyomba eria ime, na Tomas amo nabarabwo. Yeso agacha ekero ebisieri bisiekire, agatenena gati‐gati, akabora, “Omorembe obe asemore!”
english: A week later his disciples were in the house again, and Thomas was with them. Though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you!"

ekegusii: Korende omokungu oria karakwe, rirorio egesusuro kebe obogima ase obogima,
english: But if there is serious injury, you are to take life for life,

ekegusii: “Naki ndakore mbaabere? Abana baino bantigire, nigo bagotiana ase chinyasae ching’ao. Ekero nabaete ebinto biisaine nigo babete bagotomana, bakagenda ase chinyomba chi’abakungu abanyaka.
